title: Compactness of a constructible sheaf against uniformly bounded families
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All sheaves below are $\Lambda_X$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and all Hom groups and direct sums are in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In particular no derived-completion condition is imposed.

Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of filtered colimits of constructible sheaves computed in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, and
$$
\Dic(X,\Lambda)=\{K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X}):H^n(K)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\text{ for all }n\in\mathbf Z\}.
$$
Let $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, viewed as a complex concentrated in degree $0$, let $a\le b$ be integers, let $I$ be a small set in the fixed universe, and let $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in I}$ be a family in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ with $H^n(K_\lambda)=0$ for $n\notin[a,b]$ and every $\lambda$. Then for every $s\in\mathbf Z$ the natural homomorphism
$$
\alpha_s:\bigoplus_{\lambda\in I}\Hom(C,K_\lambda[s])\longrightarrow\Hom\bigl(C,(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in I}K_\lambda)[s]\bigr),\qquad (f_\lambda)\longmapsto\sum_\lambda\iota_\lambda[s]\circ f_\lambda,
$$
is an isomorphism. The sum in this formula is finite because $(f_\lambda)$ has finite support, and $\iota_\lambda$ denotes the coprojection. The shift convention is $(K[s])^n=K^{n+s}$.

proof.text: Derive that X is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact from finite type over the field. Apply localizingClosure_exists to the empty generating class to obtain all required derived coproducts and coproducts of distinguished triangles. Choose any colimit cofan of K. Prove the assertion simultaneously for all shifts by strong induction on the nonnegative integer b-a.

When a=b, apply the single-degree comparison to the chosen cofan, with the given ind-constructible degree-a cohomology. This applies to both coefficient objects and to the arbitrary HasDerivedCategory presentation fixed in the statement.

When a<b, use the canonical standard-t-structure triangle truncLT(b) K_i -> K_i -> truncGE(b) K_i. The first vertex is in [a,b-1] and the third in [b,b]. The cohomology exact sequence identifies the first vertex cohomology with H^q K_i in [a,b-1] and the third vertex degree-b cohomology with H^b K_i. Transport ind-constructibility along these isomorphisms. No closure assertion about the cohomology of the sum is needed.

Take the coproduct triangle with its specified vertex coproduct cofans and coprojection morphisms. The first-vertex comparisons are bijective by the induction hypothesis and the third-vertex comparisons by the base case.

Apply the homological preadditive coyoneda functor and its shift sequence to obtain the five-term exact sequences B[s-1] -> A[s] -> K[s] -> B[s] -> A[s+1]. Their direct sum is exact: define a componentwise lift sending zero to zero, choosing preimages in every kernel, and map finitely supported tuples by this zero-preserving lift. Naturality of the homology connecting morphisms and of the other triangle arrows proves all four comparison squares commute. The additive five lemma makes the middle comparison bijective. Finally transport along the unique coproduct isomorphism from the chosen cofan to the middle-vertex cofan; its coprojection equations identify the transported map with the original comparison.
